title: How to Love (Mindfulness Essentials, #3)
author: Thich Nhat Hanh
myRating: 1 of 5 stars 2 of 5 stars 3 of 5 stars 4 of 5 stars [ 5 of 5 stars ]
reviewText: i listen to thich nhat hanh whenever i have a personal crash out. calming meditations on the art of living love, creating happiness, and being mindful: how love is rooted in understanding, how being in nature brings us closer to love, how love is not perfection. also sweet notes on "home": in vietnamese, partners are referred to as "home" ("my home cooked this meal; i cooked this meal for my home"); we must learn to come home to ourselves; home is within us and our loved ones

title: What I Talk About When I Talk About Running
author: Murakami, Haruki
myRating: 1 of 5 stars 2 of 5 stars [ 3 of 5 stars ] 4 of 5 stars 5 of 5 stars
reviewText: my first murakami, not inspired to read more tbh. listened to this on my runs this month and it was interesting at first (running as a way to create a void, the meditative nature of pain and solitude, the connection between body and mind as a writer/intellectual) but then he started talking about harvard undergrads weirdly and everything after that was repetitive. meh... this is why i don't read books by men

title: How to Stand Up to a Dictator
author: Ressa, Maria A.
myRating: 1 of 5 stars 2 of 5 stars 3 of 5 stars 4 of 5 stars [ 5 of 5 stars ]
reviewText:
"the struggle of man against power is the struggle of memory against forgetting"-- in her autobiography, maria ressa helps us remember the history of political abuse in the philippines, and why we must fight to change it. i thought i could not idolize her more but here i am an even bigger admirer. 
 
 this book was sooooo insanely incredible and inspirational, a reminder of the people who have been and are doing the work to fight tyranny and oppression, something i have to hold onto right now. i listened to the audiobook, which is narrated by maria ressa herself, and it made me cry multiple times. her writing is brave, precise, and rooted in love for the philippines and its people; her life story is unimaginable. i feel renewed after finishing, 1000% recommend
